judged_text: The backfill interpolates each migrated host value directly into an INSERT statement (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), so any host string containing a single quote breaks or injects. A legacy embeddable_hosts value like `o'brien.example.com` (accepted by the old free-text setting) makes the migration raise a SQL syntax error on deploy; crafted values execute arbitrary SQL.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` builds raw SQL with unescaped interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If `h` contains a single quote, it will break SQL syntax, and because it’s executed as SQL text it also enables SQL injection from the stored `site_settings` value. This is directly verifiable from the diff.
